item.title: Dhaka, Tokyo to upgrade BIG-B into ‘BIG-B for Shared Prosperity’
item.description:
In light of the rapidly changing global situation, a more prevalent supply chain risk, rapid technological innovation and mounting social issues, Bangladesh and Japan will upgrade BIG-B into “BIG-B for Shared Prosperity” as an initiative of “strategic cooperation” in the exclusive partnership between the two countries.
This is aimed at enhancing the resilience and preserving each country’s freedom of decision, said the Japanese government.
Meanwhile, Bangladesh and Japan signed a number of Memoranda of Cooperation and other documents between the two countries, said the Japanese side.
The two countries signed five cooperation documents covering economic relations and the business environment, agriculture, fisheries and livestock, and environmental protection.
These include a memorandum of cooperation between Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and Bangladesh’s Economic Relations Division; separate memoranda between Japan’s Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries and Bangladesh’s Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock; a memorandum of cooperation on the environment between Japan’s Ministry of the Environment and Bangladesh’s Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change; and a letter of intent between Japan’s Global Environment Bureau and Bangladesh’s Department of Environment under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
BIG-B (the Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt) is an economic development initiative with three pillars: (1) economic infrastructure development, (2) improvement of the investment environment, (3) strengthening connectivity.
It has served as the flagship initiative of Japan-Bangladesh cooperation and has long supported Bangladesh’s economic growth.
The “BIG-B for Shared Prosperity” positions Bangladesh as a hub to promote common prosperity and to contribute to mutual growth, said the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Japan and Bangladesh have agreed to strengthen cooperation in connectivity, energy security, disaster resilience, trade, investment and defence to promote economic growth and regional peace and stability.
Under the proposed cooperation framework, the two countries will promote integrated economic infrastructure development centred on Matarbari Deep-Sea Port, including power and energy facilities, airports, roads, railways, inland waterways and special economic zones, to strengthen supply chains and develop Bangladesh into a logistics and industrial hub.
They will also work to improve the investment climate, develop human resources, expand public-private partnerships and establish transparent and predictable rules to attract investment.
Both sides will seek to expand trade and investment under the Japan-Bangladesh Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA), improve market access and promote industrial upgrading and export diversification.
The cooperation will also focus on building resilient supply chains in manufacturing, logistics, food and agriculture, information and communication technology, pharmaceuticals and other sectors.
To strengthen energy security, the two countries will promote initiatives under Japan's “POWERR Asia” framework for a stable and economically viable energy supply and explore opportunities for energy infrastructure development in the Matarbari region.
They will also enhance cooperation to address natural disasters and climate change, including strengthening emergency response capabilities and developing sustainable disaster-prevention infrastructure.
In the security sector, Japan will support Bangladesh's capacity-building efforts and promote bilateral security and defence cooperation, with a focus on maritime security, maritime domain awareness, coastal patrols and port security.
The framework includes providing patrol boats to Bangladesh under Japan's first Official Security Assistance (OSA) project, exploring a second OSA project and providing patrol vessels through official development assistance (ODA) to strengthen coastal security capabilities.
Both countries will also work to improve their ability to respond to emerging technological challenges, including cybersecurity, as part of broader efforts to enhance resilience against geopolitical uncertainties and promote peace and stability.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen bilateral relations under the two countries’ Strategic Partnership, with a focus on regional peace, prosperity and stability.
At a summit meeting in Japan, Takaichi congratulated Tarique Rahman on assuming office as prime minister and described Bangladesh as a friend that shares the values of democracy.
Amid growing international instability, she said Japan strongly supports Bangladesh’s ability to make its own decisions freely and strengthen its resilience under Japan’s updated “Free and Open Indo-Pacific” (FOIP) vision.
Takaichi also expressed her intention to work with Tarique Rahman to promote peace and prosperity in the region.
In response, Tarique Rahman said Japan, as a peace-loving nation, was among the first countries to recognise Bangladesh’s independence and holds a special place in the hearts of the Bangladeshi people.
He said the two countries had built longstanding friendly relations and expressed his commitment to working with Takaichi to take bilateral ties to new heights.
The two leaders held the summit meeting on October 27 from 11:45am for around 25 minutes, followed by a joint press event and luncheon, according to the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Tarique says Rohingya crisis can only be resolved in Myanmar
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday said a lasting solution to the Rohingya crisis lies in Myanmar, stressing that forcibly displaced Rohingyas must be able to return to their homeland voluntarily, safely, swiftly and with dignity.
“The lasting solution to the (Rohingya) crisis lies in Myanmar,” he said during a bilateral summit with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi at the Kantei (the Japanese Prime Minister’s Office) in Tokyo.
Tarique expressed deep concerns over the deteriorating situation in Myanmar and the resulting displacement of Rohingya people, said Prime Minister's Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Hossain Shadhin.
He called for an end to all forms of violence, unhindered humanitarian assistance and dialogue among all parties concerned to resolve the crisis.
The prime minister appreciated Japan’s support for Bangladesh’s humanitarian efforts for Rohingyas, who were forcibly displaced from Myanmar’s Rakhine State and took shelter in Bangladesh.
He also urged Japan to remain actively engaged with all parties to help establish peace and stability in Rakhine.
During the summit, the two leaders emphasised strengthening long-standing Bangladesh-Japan relations, expanding trade and investment, and enhancing cooperation in energy security, technology, space research, infrastructure and regional and international affairs.
Tarique Rahman called for greater engagement by the Japanese government and private sector in Bangladesh’s economic development, technological advancement and industrialisation.
He also recalled the visits to Japan by his father, late president Ziaur Rahman, and the contributions of his mother, former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia, to strengthening bilateral ties, pledging to build on their legacy and take relations between the two countries to a new level.
The prime minister highlighted the two countries’ shared commitment to multilateralism, international peace and respect for international law.
He thanked Japan for supporting Bangladesh Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman’s election as president of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.
Tarique expressed his desire to work closely with Japan to strengthen multilateral cooperation and address global challenges during the session.
Reaffirming their shared vision of a free, open, peaceful and inclusive Indo-Pacific, he stressed greater cooperation in regional connectivity, the free flow of trade and economic growth.
Outlining Bangladesh’s ambition to become a regional hub for the economy, technology and manufacturing, the prime minister said the country can become the world’s ninth-largest consumer economy by 2030, while its gross domestic product can exceed US$1 trillion by 2034.
He said Japan holds a special place in the hearts of the people of Bangladesh and recalled that it was among the first countries to recognise Bangladesh after its independence in 1971. Japan has since remained one of Bangladesh’s key development partners for more than five decades.
The bilateral summit between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi began at 11:45am local time at the Kantei.
The meeting followed a formal welcome at 11:30am, a guard of honour and the introduction of the two leaders’ respective delegations.
During the meeting, Tarique invited Takaichi to visit Bangladesh at a mutually convenient time, expressing hope that the long-standing friendship between the two countries will continue to deepen through mutual trust, cooperation and shared prosperity.

item.title: Zahed: BNP won’t back extrajudicial killings
item.description:
The BNP fought against enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings over the past 17 years and will not backtrack on that position after forming the government, Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman said on Tuesday, adding that the prime minister will take the final decision about the inspector general of police over his crossfire remarks.
“If a state or government kills someone extrajudicially, it ceases to function as a state and behaves like a thug,” Zahed said while speaking at a press briefing on the progress of various government activities at the Secretariat.
No democratic government can support extrajudicial killings, he said, stressing that the state must arrest criminals and hand them over to the judicial system for trial.
“Anyone can commit murder. A state becomes a state when it exercises the authority to deliver justice,” he added.
A death sentence can be imposed through judicial proceedings, but extrajudicial killing can never be an act of the state, the adviser said, adding that the state can arrest an accused person and hand them over to the judiciary, exercising the executive authority and laws can be amended, if necessary, but there can be no scope for extrajudicial killings.
He said the government has no intention of remaining in power after its five-year term through night-time voting or dummy elections. “It will, therefore, avoid any action that can damage its credibility, as incidents such as extrajudicial killings will undermine public confidence in the government.”
Asked about IGP Md Ali Hossain Fakir’s remarks that crossfire operations could be carried out if the government gives permission, Zahed said he believed the police chief retreated from his earlier position in subsequent remarks. “He also stepped back from serious allegations he made about journalists in general,” he said, adding that he thought the issue should now be put to rest.
Asked whether the IGP should be allowed to remain in office even after clarifying his remarks, he said the matter is for journalists to assess.
The adviser said he felt the situation would have been problematic had the police chief continued to stand by his earlier statement.
He also stressed that government officials are not obliged to carry out illegal orders and public servants must perform their duties in accordance with the law.
Zahed also said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will take the final decision about the IGP after returning from the Japan visit.
Responding to a question about the arrest of a woman entrepreneur in Bhaluka, Mymensingh, for regretting voting for the BNP on Facebook live, he said he did not consider the position taken by local BNP activists who protested against her remarks to be justified.
Police took the woman into custody following the protests and later sent her to court under Section 151 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Zahed said people have the right to express such views. “Many people in Bangladesh, including some who make offensive remarks about the Prime Minister, are expressing their opinions without facing similar action,” he said, adding that such remarks can certainly be made.
He, however, said the matter is now within the jurisdiction of the judiciary, expressing hope that investigators will not treat the woman’s remarks as a criminal offence.
Asked about the reported vandalism and looting of the homes of three Hindu families in Pirganj, Rangpur, the adviser said he heard that police were deployed and action was taken in this regard.
He said there was a tendency among some extremist groups in Bangladesh to act aggressively. “Such tendencies increased during the interim government’s tenure, and appropriate action was not taken against such incidents in many cases,” he added.
Zahed also assured that the current government will take action against such crimes. “You cannot expect to remain beyond the reach of justice under this government. I assure you of that,” he said.
Members of the Hindu community also want to live safely in a liberal democratic country, he said, adding that people have expectations from political parties entrusted with governing the country, and the BNP will have to fulfil those expectations.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,240 as 7 die in 24 hours
item.description:
Seven more children died with measles and measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours to 8am on Tuesday, bringing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,240 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified six latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths while another as a confirmed measles death.
With these, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,136, while confirmed deaths from measles stood at 105.
A total of 1,232 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, bringing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 223,784.
Meanwhile, 63 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 23,541.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 199,127 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 191,090 have recovered, according to DGHS data.

item.title: HC gives task force six more months to probe Sagar-Runi murder
item.description:
The High Court has granted a task force investigating the murders of journalist couple Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi another six months to complete its probe.
The court also summoned the task force chief and Tanvir Zoha, an information technology expert and prosecutor at the International Crimes Tribunal, to provide an update on the investigation on April 27 next year. They have been directed to appear with relevant documents, and the court will hear their statements in camera.
A High Court bench comprising Justice Shikder Md Mahmudur Razi and Justice Fatema Anwar passed the order on Tuesday.
Senior lawyers Monzil Morshed and Shishir Manir appeared for the couple's family, while Attorney General Ruhul Quddus Kazal represented the state.
On September 30, 2024, the High Court ordered the removal of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) from the investigation and directed the formation of a high-level task force under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The court set April 6, 2025, as the deadline for submitting the investigation report.
The ministry subsequently formed the task force. However, the investigation did not progress as scheduled, as the High Court was on vacation on the designated date. The state later sought additional time, and the case was placed on the High Court's hearing list again.
Sagar, news editor of Maasranga Television, and Runi, a senior reporter at ATN Bangla, were murdered at their rented apartment in the capital's West Rajabazar area on the night of February 11, 2012. Their only son, Mahir Sarowar Megh, was at home at the time.
Runi's brother, Nausher Ali Roman, filed a murder case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station. Local police initially investigated the case before it was transferred to the Detective Branch three days later.
After the Detective Branch failed to make progress, the case was handed over to RAB on April 18, 2012.

item.title: IRRI, govt move to strengthen methane emissions monitoring in rice production
item.description:
The International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) has brought together government agencies, researchers and development partners in Dhaka for a two-day workshop aimed at strengthening Bangladesh’s capacity to measure, report and verify greenhouse gas emissions from rice cultivation.
The workshop, held on October 27–28, focuses on developing a national measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) system and advancing a methane mitigation roadmap for the rice sector.
Organized under the Accelerating the Scaling of Low-emissions Rice Production in Southeast Asia (AcceLER) project and CGIAR’s Climate Action and Scaling for Impact science programs, the event seeks to improve emissions tracking and institutional coordination.
Rice cultivation supports approximately 13 million farming households in Bangladesh but is also a major source of agricultural methane emissions.
Addressing the workshop, Agriculture Secretary Md Salim Khan emphasized the need to reduce emissions without compromising food security or farmers’ livelihoods.
“What we cannot measure, we cannot manage,” he said, adding that a transparent MRV system would strengthen Bangladesh’s greenhouse gas inventory and reporting under its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), while creating opportunities for climate finance.
Department of Agricultural Extension Director General Md Abdur Rahim stressed the importance of reliable data systems for expanding climate-smart agricultural practices and accessing international climate finance.
Bangladesh Rice Research Institute Director General Dr Md Rafiqul Islam said the proposed MRV system must be cost-effective, scalable and transparent.
He identified alternate wetting and drying (AWD), climate-smart rice varieties, improved fertilizer management, direct-seeded rice and better residue management as potential measures to reduce emissions.
IRRI Bangladesh Country Representative Dr Humnath Bhandari highlighted the potential of digital MRV systems to provide reliable emissions data at farm, project and national levels.
IRRI Senior Scientist Dr Bjoern Ole Sander said research had identified practical approaches to reducing emissions from rice production, emphasizing methane’s contribution to global warming and ground-level ozone formation.
Technical discussions examined existing agricultural reporting systems, institutional responsibilities, data gaps and a proposed national MRV framework.
Participants also reviewed experiences from Cambodia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam in promoting low-emission rice cultivation.
The workshop includes practical greenhouse gas quantification exercises using IRRI tools, alongside discussions on remote sensing, digital data management and institutional requirements.
Organizers said the initiative aims to support Bangladesh in developing a coordinated, science-based system for monitoring agricultural emissions and implementing low-emission rice production practices.

item.title: Power outage hits Secretariat, key areas of Dhaka
item.description:
A fault in the Meghnaghat-Haripur national grid line disrupted electricity supply to the Secretariat, several areas of Dhaka and parts of Chittagong on Tuesday.
The outage occurred at 12:43pm, leaving several areas of the capital without electricity.
Power Grid Bangladesh said the disruption affected areas including Bhulta, Haripur, Siddhirganj, Gulshan, Rampura, Ullon and Motijheel. Parts of Chittagong also experienced power cuts.
An official responsible for electricity at the Public Works Ministry in the Secretariat said the Dhaka Power Distribution Company Limited (DPDC) had informed him that the outage was caused by a grid failure.
Power Grid Bangladesh said the technical cause of the outage was yet to be determined. Restoration work was underway, with engineers reconnecting affected areas in phases. The national grid system is under the supervision of the National Load Despatch Centre (NLDC).
In an emergency press release, the Power Division said efforts were underway to restore electricity supply. Power was gradually returning to affected areas, with full restoration expected shortly.
Power Grid Bangladesh later announced that restoration of the national grid had been completed at 2:30pm, with all grid lines and substations operational.
The agency said electricity supply remained normal in the northern parts of the country and other unaffected areas.
Several areas of the capital, including the Secretariat and its surroundings, Moghbazar, Modhubagh, Shantinagar, Malibagh and Khilgaon, were reported to be without electricity.
In an emergency press release issued on Tuesday, the Power Division said a technical fault had disrupted electricity supply to parts of Dhaka and Chitttagong, adding that urgent efforts were underway to restore power.
Power plants were being brought back online in phases, and scattered load-shedding was expected to ease as electricity generation increased, the agency said.
It apologised for the temporary inconvenience caused by the unexpected power disruption.

item.title: Third uranium shipment reaches Rooppur plant under tight security
item.description:
The third shipment of nuclear fuel, weighing 41 tons, has reached the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant in Ishwardi, Pabna, amid tight security.
The vehicles carrying the fuel entered the plant premises around 8am on Tuesday under military escort.
The shipment arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on a special flight from Russia on Monday morning, following a stopover in Delhi, India. The fuel was packed into 12 transport containers.
In the early hours of Tuesday, the containers were loaded onto three lorries and transported by road to Rooppur. The convoy crossed the Bangabandhu Bridge and passed through Bonpara in Natore and Dashuria in Ishwardi before reaching the project site.
Police personnel were stationed at several intersections along the route to manage traffic. Members of the military, the Special Security Force (SSF) and intelligence agencies were also involved in security arrangements.
According to police and project sources, the fuel was transported from Dhaka under a special security protocol. Traffic movement along parts of the highway was temporarily restricted to prevent congestion during the convoy's passage.
Project officials said 163 uranium fuel assemblies for the plant's second unit were scheduled to arrive in seven shipments. Another 48 assemblies for refuelling the first unit were expected in two shipments. The latest consignment is the third shipment for the second unit.
Seven more flights carrying fuel from Russia are planned for November and December. The shipments are expected to transit through Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan and India.
Russia's state nuclear energy corporation, Rosatom, has said the fuel supply process is expected to be completed by December.
Fuel for the plant's first unit arrived in Bangladesh on September 29, 2023, followed by four additional shipments in October and November that year. Fuel loading in the first unit's reactor was completed in May this year.
The first unit will require the replacement of about one-fourth of its fuel after approximately 18 months of operation. A shipment of additional fuel for the unit arrived at Rooppur on October 3, while the second shipment for the second unit reached the project site on October 21.
Under the agreement, Russia will supply fuel for the plant during its first three years of operation. Bangladesh will then need to import fuel for periodic replacement.
The Rooppur plant comprises two units with a combined generation capacity of 2,400MW. Although fuel loading in the first unit has been completed, electricity generation has been delayed by technical complications.
Power generation had been expected to begin this month but was postponed following a fault in a safety valve in the automatic pressure relief system. A third round of testing on the valve was completed on September 30, and project officials began the nuclear reaction process on October 11 after receiving regulatory approval, according to project sources.
Sources said the necessary tests and procedures for the first unit, including the B-2 phase of physics testing, were completed this week. The reports have been submitted to the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) for review.
After receiving final approval, the unit is expected to move to Stage C, or power startup, a key phase before electricity generation. During this stage, the plant's systems will undergo comprehensive testing to verify their functionality.

item.title: Sajek residents demand probe into attack on blockade
item.description:
Sajek residents and local organizations have demanded punishment for those responsible for an alleged attack on a peaceful road blockade on October 22, compensation for affected traders and withdrawal of a case against protesters.
In a memorandum submitted to the government on Monday, the Sajek Public Rights Protection Committee and Sajek Karbari Association also demanded an impartial judicial inquiry into the incident and the removal of armed members of the Santu Larma-led faction of the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Samhati Samiti (PCJSS) from the area, said a press release.
The signatories alleged that the armed group had been threatening residents, firing indiscriminately and extorting money from Jhum cultivators, creating fear and insecurity in several villages.
According to the statement, the group began armed activities in the area on August 31. Its members allegedly demanded Tk1,000 for every ari of Jhum land and extorted money from owners of rice-processing machines, turmeric-grinding machines and engine-powered boats. A nine-year-old girl, Kosmita Tripura, was reportedly injured by gunfire.
Residents said they had repeatedly urged the local military administration to take action against the group but received no effective response. They began an indefinite road blockade on October 11, temporarily suspending it after the army sought additional time. The blockade resumed on October 15, was suspended for Durga Puja and restarted on October 22.
The signatories alleged that security personnel attacked protesters with batons without provocation while discussions were underway about allowing stranded tourists to pass. Army personnel subsequently opened fire, vandalised and looted shops and homes in Ujopazar, and injured several people, they claimed.
They also alleged that army and police personnel later attempted to arrest SSC examinee Jharna Chakma over her participation in the blockade.
The memorandum was signed by Babudhan Chakma, convener of the Sajek Public Rights Protection Committee; Natun Joy Chakma, president of the Sajek Karbari Association; Ushatan Chakma of the Student-People's Struggle Council; Jiko Chakma of the Sajek Public Rights Protection Committee; and Sadhana Debi Chakma of Sajek Women's Society.

item.title: Article 9 Committee launched to ensure accessibility for persons with disabilities
item.description:
A new advocacy platform, the Article 9 Committee, has been launched to promote the implementation of Article 9 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD), which requires measures to ensure accessibility for persons with disabilities across all areas of life.
The committee held its inaugural meeting at the Omni Residency Hotel in Baridhara, Dhaka, on Monday, with a focus on addressing barriers in infrastructure, transport, information and communication technology, and public services.
The meeting was organized by the women-led Bangladesh Society for the Change and Advocacy Nexus (B-SCAN), with support from the Centre for Services and Information on Disability (CSID) and the Centre for Disabilities in Development (CDD), under the Disability Inclusive Civic Engagement (DiCE) project. The project is supported by the Nagorikata – Civic Engagement Fund, managed by GFA.
Article 9 of the UNCRPD calls on states to ensure that persons with disabilities can access the physical environment, transportation, information and communications, and other facilities and services open or provided to the public on an equal basis with others. Accessibility is essential to independent living and full participation in society.
Representatives attend the inaugural meeting of the Article 9 Committee, formed to promote accessibility for persons with disabilities, in Baridhara, Dhaka, on Monday, October 26, 2026. Photo: Courtesy
The committee aims to raise awareness of accessibility rights, bring together organisations of persons with disabilities, civil society groups, development organisations, professional bodies and academic institutions, and strengthen coordination and accountability in implementing accessibility standards.
Accessibility extends beyond ramps to include accessible buildings and toilets, public transport, websites, sign language and information in accessible formats. Universal design can also benefit older people, children, pregnant women and those with temporary mobility difficulties.
B-SCAN Executive Director Salma Mahbub said the platform would work nationally to make Bangladesh accessible to all by combining the knowledge and experience of civil society organisations.
The committee's initial priorities include identifying barriers across infrastructure, transport, communication technologies and services; engaging responsible institutions; and advocating for universal design to make accessibility an integral part of planning and service delivery.
Representatives from B-SCAN, CDD and CSID attended the meeting, alongside those from WaterAid, Bangladesh Poribesh Andolon (BAPA), the Bangladesh Institute of Planners (BIP), Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST), BRAC, Friendship, SERAC, WBB Trust, the Women with Disabilities Development Foundation (WDDF), SMF, the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI), and Mass Studio.

item.title: Persons with disabilities demand immediate anti-discrimination law
item.description:
Persons with disabilities and rights advocates have urged the government to immediately enact a comprehensive anti-discrimination law to ensure inclusion, protection and equal rights for all marginalized communities.
The call came at a consultation organized jointly by the Centre for Disabilities in Development (CDD) and Manusher Jonno Foundation (MJF) at the Shakti Foundation Training and Research Center in Akran, Savar, on Tuesday.
Held under the Disability Inclusive Civic Engagement (DiCE) project, the consultation brought together persons with disabilities, civil society representatives and government officials to review the draft Anti-Discrimination Bill and propose recommendations from a disability rights perspective.
The project is funded by Switzerland, Canada and the European Union, implemented through GFA Consulting Group GmbH and supported by the Nagorikata – Civic Engagement Fund.
Wasiur Rahman Tonmoy, lead – Youth & Social Cohesion at MJF, presented the keynote paper, outlining discrimination faced by marginalized groups in education, healthcare, employment and public and private services. These groups include Dalits, Indigenous people in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, tea garden workers and persons with disabilities.
KM Shahiduzzaman, upazila social services officer in Savar, attended as chief guest and stressed the need for enforceable legal protections and coordination between government agencies and non-governmental organisations to improve access to essential services.
Advocate Ruma Sultana, programme coordinator at MJF, highlighted the need for continued consultations with diverse communities to refine the proposed legislation. She was involved in drafting the initial Anti-Discrimination Bill, 2022.
Umme Farhana Zarif Kanta, deputy director and team lead for PROKAS at Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST), called for stronger partnerships with grassroots organizations to ensure persons with disabilities are represented in legislative advocacy.
The consultation included 48 persons with disabilities: 25 with visual impairments, 14 with physical disabilities, seven with hearing impairments and two with cerebral palsy. Sign language interpretation was provided by Iftekhar Ahmed Shorful.
Facilitated by Tonmoy, participants worked in five groups to review the draft bill and develop recommendations.
They called for the legislation to be enacted under the title “Anti-Discrimination Law” and for its definitions of discrimination to be aligned with existing national laws and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD).
Other recommendations included incorporating relevant provisions of the Rights and Protection of Persons with Disabilities Act 2013 into the proposed law, ensuring representation of persons with disabilities on monitoring committees and the proposed National Anti-Discrimination Commission, and simplifying complaint procedures and access to legal aid.
Participants also called for effective enforcement and accountability mechanisms covering both public and private sectors.
Anika Rahman Lipy, assistant director of training at CDD, delivered the closing remarks and vote of thanks. Participants pledged to continue engaging with policymakers to advance the proposed law.

item.title: Man jailed for embezzling Tk6 crore in Rajuk plot scam
item.description:
A Dhaka court has sent Munshi Manzur-e-Elahi, also known as Manjurul Alam, to jail after rejecting his bail petition in a case over the alleged embezzlement of Tk6.23 crore from a businessman by promising to arrange a five-katha Rajuk plot in Uttara.
Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Md Zakir Hossain passed the order on Tuesday. Abdulllah Al Mamun, a lawyer for the complainant, confirmed the matter.
According to the case statement, the complainant, Md Nasir, proprietor of Prashanti Enterprise, knew the accused and had been involved in a joint land trading business with them in Dhaka.
Under an oral agreement, Nasir was entitled to 50% of the profits from land sales, with the remaining half going to the accused.
The accused allegedly told Nasir that a five-katha Rajuk plot was available in Uttara for Tk5–6 crore and could later be sold for Tk9–10 crore. Persuaded by the offer, Nasir visited the plot on August 1, 2023, and agreed to invest.
The complaint alleges that the accused subsequently collected Tk6.23 crore from Nasir in instalments through pay orders and cash, claiming the money was needed for the advance payment and registration of the land.
Several crore taka were transferred through pay orders issued by City Bank and IFIC Bank in favour of Md Robiul Alam, proprietor of Rafin Enterprise, and another accused, Munshi Manzur-e-Elahi.
Other alleged members of the group, including Rafiqul Islam, Md Anisur Rahman Mia Hasib, Hasna Hena and Asif Hasan Tulip, also collected cash from Nasir at different times, according to the complaint.
Despite receiving the money, the accused allegedly delayed handing over the plot. They later stopped answering Nasir's calls and vacated their office in Sector 16 of Uttara after locking it, the complaint says.
When Nasir sought a refund on December 1, 2024, the accused allegedly refused to return the money.
Nasir filed a Complaint Register (CR) case with the court on December 29, 2024. The court took cognisance of the case the same day and directed the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to investigate. Following the investigation, the CID submitted its report on June 30 this year.
Meanwhile, victims formed a human chain on the court premises from Tuesday morning until afternoon, demanding Manjurul Alam's trial.
They also called for the swift arrest of other alleged members of the fraud syndicate, the recovery of the money and stronger intervention by the authorities.

item.title: Fire erupts from ground in Cox’s Bazar, three units deployed
item.description:
A fire broke out from the ground in Inani, a tourist area in Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar, while workers were excavating the site to install a tube well on Tuesday. Smoke and a gas-like smell were also reported, raising suspicions that underground gas may have fuelled the blaze.
Three fire service units were deployed to the site and were working to bring the fire under control.
The fire erupted around 8:30am near a small bridge in Inani.
Saidul Islam, station officer at Ukhiya Fire Service, confirmed the incident, saying firefighters reached the scene after receiving the report. He said the cause of the fire was still being investigated, although the preliminary suspicion was that gas beneath the surface might be responsible.
Meanwhile, electricity supply along a 15km stretch of the 33kV power line, from Monkhali to Patuartek, was temporarily suspended over concerns that the fire could spread to electrical infrastructure, according to Ukhiya Palli Bidyut Samity.
The incident triggered panic among local residents.
Al-Amin, an employee of a five-star hotel near the site, said several hotel staff members lived in a room beside the area where the fire broke out.
“The fire service has arrived. Seeing the fire suddenly was truly terrifying,” he said.

item.title: Tarique, Takaichi begin bilateral summit in Tokyo
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and his Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi began their bilateral summit in Tokyo on Tuesday to strengthen the two countries’ strategic partnership, boost trade and investment, and expand cooperation in key sectors.
The talks began at 11:45am local time at the Japanese Prime Minister’s Office, known as the Kantei.
Earlier, Takaichi warmly welcomed Tarique at the Kantei upon his arrival. A contingent of the Japanese armed forces also accorded him a guard of honour.
After the ceremony, Takaichi introduced members of her cabinet to Tarique, who in turn introduced the members of his delegation to the Japanese Prime Minister.
The two leaders are scheduled to hold talks until 12:10pm. They will make a joint announcement on the outcome of their talks at 12:15pm.
Takaichi will later host a luncheon in honour of Tarique from 12:30pm to 1:10pm.
At the beginning of the lunch, she is scheduled to deliver a brief welcome remark and propose a toast, followed by a short reply and return toast from Tarique.
According to Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Hossain Shadhin, the two leaders will discuss strengthening bilateral relations, expanding business, trade and investment, Japanese cooperation in various sectors and international issues.
The two sides are also expected to explore cooperation in renewable energy, agriculture, science and technology, digital transformation, skills development and human resource development.
Tarique is leading a high-level delegation comprising Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Finance and Planning Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit and Prime Minister’s Adviser on Posts, Telecommunications, ICT and Science and Technology Rehan Asif Asad.
Other delegation members include Invest Bangladesh Authority Chairman Ashik Chowdhury, Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman, Prime Minister’s Special Assistant for Overseas Employment in Asia-Pacific Region Dr Md Shakirul Islam Khan, Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam, Secretary Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury, Economic Relations Division Secretary Shahriar Kader Siddiky and Prime Minister’s Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon.
Hefazat-e-Islam Joint Secretary General and Nezame Islam Party acting Secretary General Azizul Haque Islamabadi and Am Janatar Dal General Secretary Md Tarek Rahman are also accompanying the Prime Minister.
The two countries’ national flags were displayed along the road leading to the Japanese Prime Minister’s Office to welcome Tarique.
Tarique then signed the visitors’ book at the entrance to the main hall of the building before the two leaders sat down for bilateral talks.
The Prime Minister arrived in Tokyo on Monday morning on a four-day visit at the invitation of Takaichi.
He was received at Narita International Airport by Japanese State Minister for Foreign Affairs Nakasone Yasutaka.
This is Tarique’s third state visit abroad since taking office on February 17 this year. He previously visited Malaysia and China on state visits and travelled to New York, the United States, in September to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

item.title: Sagar-Runi murder: Task force seeks more time to submit report
item.description:
A high-level task force formed under the Ministry of Home Affairs is verifying information gathered from various sources in connection with the murder of journalist couple Sagar Sarwar and Meherun Runi. The task force has sought more time from the High Court to submit its investigation report.
A progress report outlining the status of the investigation has already been submitted to the court.
The investigation report was scheduled to be submitted on Tuesday. The matter is before a High Court bench comprising Justice Shikdar Mahmudur Razi and Justice Fatema Anwar.
Ahead of the deadline, the task force filed an application for an extension, saying in its progress report that it was still verifying several pieces of information.
On September 30, 2024, the High Court ordered the removal of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) from the investigation and directed the formation of a high-level task force under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The court initially set April 6, 2025, as the deadline for submitting the investigation report. The ministry subsequently formed the task force in line with the directive.
The report could not be submitted on the scheduled date, and the court later granted three six-month extensions following applications by the state, on April 22, October 23 and April 26. The case has now appeared on the High Court’s cause list again.
Sagar Sarwar, news editor at Maasranga Television, and Meherun Runi, a senior reporter at ATN Bangla, were murdered at their rented apartment in Dhaka’s West Rajabazar on the night of February 11, 2012. Their bodies were discovered the following morning.
The following day, Runi’s brother, Nausher Ali Roman, filed a murder case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station.
More than 14 years after the murders, the investigation report remains pending despite changes in the investigators and the formation of a high-level task force.

item.title: IFAD, partners support agritech startups to help small-scale farmers
item.description:
The International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) and the German Sparkassenstiftung for International Cooperation (DSIK) recently brought together startups, public institutions, market actors and development partners in Dhaka for the Innovatech Bangladesh Demo Day, marking the end of the programme's first cycle in Asia.
Funded by IFAD and the European Union and implemented by Sparkassenstiftung, Innovatech helps startups adapt, test and strengthen digital solutions for small-scale farmers.
In Bangladesh, two agritech startups, Agronochain and Krishi Shwapno, tested their solutions in the field alongside projects funded by IFAD and the government. The startups worked with the Palli Karma-Sahayak Foundation (PKSF) and the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE).
At the Demo Day, the startups presented their implementation experiences, results and lessons. An accompanying panel discussion examined how institutions, market actors and financing mechanisms could work together to help solutions succeed in rural Bangladesh, move beyond pilot projects and reach more farmers.
“Transforming rural Bangladesh at the scale needed demands strong partnerships between government, innovators and the private sector,” said Valantine Achancho, IFAD country director for Bangladesh.
“Programmes like Innovatech complement public investment by bringing practical, market-driven solutions to rural communities. By testing new ideas and reducing investment risks, they help promising innovations grow into solutions that deliver lasting benefits for smallholder farmers and rural entrepreneurs,” he added.
“Rural areas do not need technology for technology’s sake. They need solutions that address a specific problem, work under the real conditions faced by producers and remain relevant after the project ends,” said Christina Olsen, director of Innovatech.
“At Innovatech, we start with demand and then bring startups and producers together so that solutions are adapted to the people who will actually use them,” she added.
The panel discussions highlighted that technology alone is rarely the main obstacle to expanding digital solutions in rural areas.
Moving from pilot projects to wider adoption requires genuine demand from rural communities, institutions willing to adopt the solutions, viable business models, market access and clear arrangements for financing and ownership after project support ends. The discussions also emphasised the need to engage the private sector as a full partner.
Bangladesh is part of Innovatech 2.0, which, between 2024 and 2026, helped more than 32,000 rural households in Bangladesh, Bolivia, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Peru access digital solutions developed by 15 technology startups.
The solutions help rural households connect with markets and financial services, manage crops, improve traceability and adopt more sustainable practices.
The programme connected the startups with 811 rural organisations, with nearly 17,000 women and more than 11,300 young people participating. Two out of every three participating producer organisations adopted agroecological practices.
Across its two editions, Innovatech has supported around 30 startups whose solutions have benefited more than 50,000 rural households.

Court imposes travel ban on two 38th BCS candidates
item.description:
A Dhaka court has imposed travel bans on Sanjay Das, recommended for the administration cadre, and Abu Saleh Md Musa, recommended for the foreign service cadre, in connection with a corruption case involving alleged fraud in the 38th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) examination.
Dhaka Metropolitan Senior Special Judge Shahjahan Kabir issued the orders on Tuesday following separate applications filed by the investigating officer.
Akhtarul Islam, public relations officer of the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), confirmed the development.
The applications were filed by ACC Assistant Director Sajjad Hossain, the investigating officer in the case.
According to the applications, the accused allegedly used forged documents to secure government jobs for personal gain, misleading the Bangladesh Public Service Commission (BPSC) about their eligibility.
As a result, Das was recommended for the administration cadre and Musa for the foreign service cadre through the 38th BCS examination.
A case was subsequently filed against them over allegations that they joined government service and drew salaries and allowances by misrepresenting their eligibility, causing financial losses to the government.
The investigation is ongoing.
The applications further stated that the accused might attempt to leave the country, making travel bans necessary to facilitate the investigation.

Kane beats Yamal and Mbappe to taste Ballon d'Or glory
item.description:
Harry Kane became England's first Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.
Alexia Putellas claimed the women's prize for a third time to extend Spain's domination of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season's Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses.
The first ever Ballon d'Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late.
But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date, becoming the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001.
The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double.
He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup.
"I love to represent my country and to bring this trophy back to them and have an English winner I think is something that's really, really special, especially here in London," Kane told AFP. "What a crazy night and I'm really, really happy."
Despite being England and Tottenham's all-time record goalscorer, Kane's medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs.
He was on the losing side for Spurs in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England.
But joining Bayern in 2023 and his remarkable goalscoring consistency have earned him the highest individual award in football.
"Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career," Kane told AFP earlier. "Some people saw it as a risk but for me it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the team-mates, the team, the club and it has pushed me onto another level.
"Being a number nine for Bayern and England you are expected to score goals and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I'm really proud of," he added.
The winner in 2021 and 2022, Putellas's third Ballon d'Or caps her return to the top of the women's game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago.
Putellas succeeds Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati, the winner the past three years whose season was quashed by a leg break.
"This is a consequence of all that we achieved last season," said Putellas.
"I am really grateful for having been (at Barcelona) 14 seasons as a player, it is something incredible. It was like a perfect story."
Yamal made the boldest fashion statement of the contenders with a pink flower on the front of his black suit.
The Barcelona winger scooped up the first award of the night for young talent of the year for the third consecutive time.
But the 19-year-old fell short of becoming the youngest ever Ballon d'Or winner, finishing third, after he failed to produce his best form during Spain's World Cup success.
Mbappe finished second but his wait to win the Ballon d'Or goes on despite being the top scorer in the World Cup, Champions League and La Liga as his goals did not lead to collective triumphs for France or Real Madrid.
Luis de la Fuente beat out Paris Saint-Germain's Luis Enrique and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to be named men's coach of the year after leading Spain to World Cup glory.
"This is recognition for a job very well done over many years," De la Fuente told AFP. "I believe Spanish football, both in terms of coaching and the game itself, serves as an example of excellent youth development, which ultimately paves the way for future success."
Barcelona's Pere Romeu scooped the prize for women's coach of the year.
Paris Saint-Germain missed out on any of the main individual awards despite winning a second consecutive Champions League, but did have the consolation of men's club of the year.
Spanish duo Unai Simon and Cata Coll were named best men's and women's goalkeeper.
